A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MMTEB and contain readable main text, references, and Appendices A–H. Both have 57 pages; pages 2–57 are identical in extracted text and rendered appearance. Differences are confined to title-page metadata.

before.justification: v2 reports original embedding-model evaluations in Table 2, clustering and retrieval optimization experiments in Appendix C, and English and code benchmark results in Tables 18–19.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical evaluations unchanged, including Table 2 and the experiments and results in Appendices C and H.

M1.justification: Task selection, clustering subsampling, retrieval hard-negative sampling, and embedding caching are unchanged in Sections 2.3–2.4 and Appendices B–C. No method component or procedure is revised.

E1.justification: The multilingual, European, Indic, English, and code benchmark coverage is unchanged. Dataset construction descriptions and the task inventories in Appendices B, D, and H are identical.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain identical comparator sets, including the e5, GritLM, LaBSE, MiniLM, and MPNet models. The additional retrieval-downsampling comparators in Appendix C.1.2 are also unchanged.

E3.justification: Sampling procedures, model configurations, evaluation metrics, and Borda-count aggregation are identical. Neither the main benchmark protocols nor the supplementary experimental settings are revised.

E4.justification: Both versions contain the same synthetic-retrieval validation, clustering efficiency comparisons, retrieval-downsampling sensitivity experiments, and analyses by language speaker counts in Appendices B, C, and E.

E5.justification: Repeated-evaluation counts in Appendix B.1, the confidence interval in B.3, and clustering bootstrap distributions and significance-based rank comparisons in C.1.1 are unchanged. No statistical reporting is added or removed.

E6.justification: All result entries, rankings, and qualitative findings are identical. For example, Table 2 retains mean MTEB(Multilingual) scores of 63.2 for multilingual-e5-large-instruct and 60.9 for GritLM-7B; appendix results are likewise unchanged.

T1.justification: The task-selection formulation in Section 2.3.3 and the abstention and normalized-AUC definitions in Appendix F are identical. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion are identical. Claims about multilingual coverage, efficient benchmark construction, and smaller multilingual models outperforming larger alternatives retain the same scope.

C2.justification: Interpretations involving instruction tuning and pretraining remain unchanged. The limitations concerning English leakage, uneven language representation, and contribution-credit assignment are also identical.

D1.justification: Implementation details, model revision IDs, prompt instructions, runtime information, and code/results access information are unchanged, including Appendices C, E, and G. The title-page correspondence correction adds no technical reproducibility information.

R1.justification: Section 5 and the entire reference list are identical. No cited work or substantive positioning relative to earlier embedding benchmarks changes.

P1.justification: The title page adds Babelscape, lists Simone Tedeschi with both Sapienza and Babelscape, changes Alessia Borghini's affiliation to Babelscape, and renumbers affected affiliations. It also removes stray 'me' after the correspondence email and updates the arXiv stamp. Body language and document structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–12, Tables 1–19, their captions and placement, and the scientific-page layouts are identical. The title-page changes concern textual metadata and retain its existing layout.

improvement.justification: v3 updates affiliations and corrects the displayed correspondence email, providing limited administrative cleanup. Pages 2–57, including all scientific content and appendices, are identical. These title-page edits do not meaningfully alter the paper's overall clarity, evidential support, or reproducibility.
